I've been working this land for 30 years. I know what works here in Quzhou. The wheat-maize rotation is the backbone — reliable, I know every step of it. Cotton brings in the cash money. Some of my children work in the city now, so I have fewer hands at peak times, but I can manage 3 mu of cotton still.

For the land split: I'll put 5 mu into wheat-maize rotation — same ground, wheat in winter, maize right after harvest. That leaves 3 mu for cotton. That's 8 mu total, fits perfectly.

Wheat I plant in October. I use the improved variety from the seed station — Kenong series, same as my neighbors. Not going back to traditional seeds, yields are much lower. I water it three times: the winter water before freeze, again at jointing, again when it heads. Two sprays for aphids and mildew. After harvest in June, I put maize in immediately, hybrid seeds, no-till right into the stubble to save time and moisture. Maize practically raises itself compared to cotton.

Cotton is the hard work. I plough that ground in spring, transplant in May. Cotton needs my eye on it all season — bollworm, spider mites, aphids — so I spray 5 times. Three irrigations from the well. With fewer family hands I have to be efficient, but the cotton money is worth it.

Fertilizer I apply the way I always have. Base fertilizer before planting, then topdress at key growth stages. I don't overthink it — 30 years tells me roughly what the land needs.
